source.title: Integrated neural dynamics of sensorimotor decisions and actions.

confidence_rationale: Strong multi-region monkey recordings (PMd, M1, dlPFC, GPe, GPi; Cisek lab) showing commitment as a STATE TRANSITION off a deliberation manifold, with a rising urgency signal (baseline + slope) that sets WHEN commitment happens and pallidal activity dominated by urgency. Directly anchors MECH-090's gate-open-as-state-transition and, decisively, names the variable that sets commitment TIMING in biology -- a graded, BG-mediated urgency signal -- which is what REE's tuned refractory parameter diverges from. Mixed because it strongly SUPPORTS the latch-as-state-transition while the urgency-set timing WEAKENS any reading that a fixed refractory is the biological duration law.
failure_signatures: Commitment timing in the data is set by a graded, dynamically-rising urgency signal (BG/pallidal-mediated), not by a fixed-duration refractory. A REE latch whose release is timed by a tuned refractory parameter departs from this graded-urgency control and cannot reproduce urgency-dependent shortening/lengthening of the committed epoch.

Deciding and executing are two modes of ONE integrated dynamical system here; REE separates an E3 selection event from a downstream commit-gated routing variable, so the 'fall off the decision manifold at commitment' is modelled as a discrete gate flip rather than a continuous trajectory.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across PMd, M1, dlPFC, GPe and GPi, neural activity during a dynamic decision unfolds on a low-dimensional 'decision manifold' defined by sensory evidence and a rising urgency signal; at the moment of commitment the cortical state falls off this manifold into a choice-dependent movement trajectory. Pallidal activity during deliberation is primarily defined by urgency, consistent with a basal-ganglia-mediated gating/timing of commitment within one integrated decision-action system.
mapping.ree_translation: Commitment is the discrete transition REE models as the MECH-090 gate flipping (deliberation -> committed routing). The biological variable that sets WHEN that transition fires -- and by extension how long deliberation is maintained before commitment -- is a graded urgency signal carried prominently by the pallidum, the BG output REE's gate abstracts. MECH-342's maintenance-release (release when readiness/value degrades mid-commitment) is the de-commit-side counterpart of this graded urgency control.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Monkey reaching decisions onto an ANN commit latch. The paper's commitment is a continuous fall-off from a deliberation manifold within ONE integrated system; REE implements a discrete gate between a selection event and a routing variable. Most importantly, the urgency signal sets commitment TIMING graded-ly and dynamically; REE sets latch duration with a tuned refractory. Use this paper to anchor that biology TIMES commitment with a graded BG/urgency signal -- i.e. to justify why a fixed refractory is a divergence -- NOT to claim REE's gate matches the manifold geometry.
mapping.source_context: In vivo multi-electrode recordings, macaque monkeys, dynamic 'tokens' decision-making task with changing evidence; dimensionality reduction across 5 cortical/pallidal regions.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (PLoS Biol, Cisek lab, 5-region simultaneous analysis, recent). Mapping fidelity moderate-low: the commitment-as-state-transition maps well and the urgency-timing finding is the key divergence anchor, but REE's discrete-gate vs the paper's continuous-manifold-fall-off differ, and the urgency variable has no direct REE counterpart yet. Transfer risk moderate: macaque reaching onto ANN latch.
